Roberto Benigni rooted this devastating masterpiece in the real-life experiences of his own father, who survived a concentration camp and used humor to shield his family from the trauma. This deeply personal foundation is exactly why the film’s daring blend of slapstick comedy and unimaginable tragedy works so flawlessly without ever feeling exploitative.
⠀
Life Is Beautiful (1997), directed by Roberto Benigni, starring Roberto Benigni, Nicoletta Braschi, Giorgio Cantarini. A fiercely imaginative Jewish-Italian father uses his boundless humor to convince his young son that their harrowing imprisonment in a concentration camp is merely an elaborate, point-based game.
